notes: High overlap (5/5 shared claims: C9, C41, C87, C88, C89) on fear extinction findings. LLM finds behavioral data well-supported with adequate temporal controls. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about integration with main findings, suggesting data 'belong in a different paper' - questioning relevance rather than validity.

Exact match on 5 claims (C5, C39, C79, C122, C123) regarding astrocytic FGF2 expression. LLM finds convergent evidence across multiple methods sufficient despite marginal statistics. Peer reviewers request additional validation, expressing concern about astrocyte culture contamination and wanting in situ/IHC confirmation of astrocytic source in vivo.

4 shared claims (C8, C40, C85, C125) on FGF2 neutralization experiments. LLM finds antibody blocking evidence strong for mechanistic causality despite concentration discrepancies. Peer reviewers question antibody specificity and whether other FGF family members might be involved, despite authors showing FGF2 vs FGF1 specificity.

6 shared claims (C4, C38, C43, C48, C52, C53) on core proliferation findings. Both agree stress increases hippocampal cell proliferation with adequate controls. Peer reviewers describe study as 'thorough and interesting' without challenging proliferation data. LLM notes context-dependency limitation but overall support.

2 shared claims (C6, C62) on BLA lesion findings. Both agree stress-induced proliferation occurs independent of BLA input. Peer review suggestion to discuss BLA role in Introduction is about framing, not critique of experimental findings. LLM notes well-controlled design.

Single shared claim (C81) on FGF2 levels in conditioned media. LLM accepts that untreated ACM had no FGF2 while CORT-ACM contained 3.5 pg/ml as supporting causal mechanism. Peer reviewers request absolute quantification rather than relative levels to strengthen causal argument.

Minimal overlap (C92 only) on neuronal activation. LLM R8 focuses on cfos expression in immature neurons as mechanism. Peer R4 addresses broader behavioral findings. Limited claim overlap makes direct comparison difficult, though both relate to functional consequences.

Single shared claim (C38) on regional specificity. LLM R2 emphasizes dorsal vs ventral distinction as internal control. Peer R5 addresses broader proliferation findings. Minimal overlap but both support core proliferation data where they intersect.
Claims C74-C77 on ventral hippocampus mRNA-protein dissociation. LLM finds this unexplained and requiring further investigation. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this specific finding.
Claims C70-C73 on BDNF negative results. LLM finds this supports FGF2 specificity as mechanism. No corresponding peer review evaluation of BDNF findings.

Claims C54, C99-C101 on habituation-dependent effects. LLM notes importance for reproducibility and inverted-U hypothesis but needs validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation of habituation findings.

Claims C11, C37, C42, C137 on inverted-U phenomenon. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize and support this interpretation, requesting it be highlighted in Introduction. No direct LLM result grouping these specific claims, though LLM R10 addresses related context-dependency.
